questions.question: What is Henry Ford credited as a pioneer in?
options: Making automobiles affordable for middle-class Americans
Creating the first electric trolley system
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Ford is 'credited as a pioneer in making automobiles affordable for middle-class Americans through the system that came to be known as Fordism.'
Incorrect. The article mentions steam engines but does not credit Ford with inventing them; he worked with them on the farm.
Incorrect. The article says Ford was born in Greenfield Township, Michigan, and left home to find work in Detroit, but it does not credit him with founding Detroit.
Incorrect. The article mentions that Ford 'did not see the use of experimenting with electricity, due to the expense of trolley wires,' so he was not a pioneer of electric trolleys.

questions.question: When was the Ford Motor Company founded?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'Ford & Malcomson was reincorporated as the Ford Motor Company on June 16, 1903.'
Incorrect. 1899 is when Ford founded the Detroit Automobile Company, not the Ford Motor Company.
Incorrect. 1908 is when the Model T debuted, not when the company was founded.
Incorrect. 1911 is when Ford was awarded a patent for his transmission mechanism, not when the company was founded.

questions.question: What was the name of the first automobile Ford completed in 1896?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says, 'These experiments culminated in 1896 with the completion of a self-propelled automobile, which he named the Ford Quadricycle.'
Incorrect. The Model T debuted in 1908, much later than 1896.
Incorrect. The Ford 999 was a racer produced later, around 1902.
Incorrect. The Lincoln Model L was introduced by the Lelands in 1920, not by Ford in 1896.

questions.question: What did Henry Ford introduce into his plants in 1913?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states, 'In 1913, Ford introduced moving assembly belts into his plants, which enabled an enormous increase in production.'
Incorrect. The steering wheel was a feature of the Model T, not something introduced into plants in 1913.
Incorrect. The article mentions Ford was among the pioneers of the five-day work-week, but it does not say he introduced it in 1913.
Incorrect. The franchise system is mentioned as a business innovation, but not as something introduced into plants in 1913.

questions.question: What did Ford believe could help bring about world peace?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states, 'Ford believed that consumerism could help to bring about world peace.'
Incorrect. The article says Ford promoted the League of Nations, but it does not say he believed it would bring world peace.
Incorrect. The Ford Foundation was established after his death, and the article does not link it to world peace.
Incorrect. The five-day work-week is mentioned as a pioneering idea, but not as a path to world peace.

questions.question: Which newspaper did Ford use to promote antisemitism in the 1920s?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says, 'In the 1920s, Ford promoted antisemitism through his newspaper The Dearborn Independent.'
Incorrect. The article does not mention The Detroit Free Press.
Incorrect. The article does not mention The New York Times.
Incorrect. The article does not mention The Ford Times.

questions.question: What was the price of the Model T when it debuted in 1908?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states, 'It was so inexpensive at $825 in 1908 ($29,560 today), with the price falling every year.'
Incorrect. $360 was the price in 1916, not at the debut in 1908.
Incorrect. $28,000 was the capital of the Ford Motor Company, not the price of a car.
Incorrect. $160,000 was the value of parts supplied by the Dodge brothers, not the price of a car.

questions.question: What color were all new Model Ts after the development of the assembly line?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article quotes Ford: 'Any customer can have a car painted any color that he wants so long as it is black.' It also explains that the assembly line mandated black because of quicker drying time.
Incorrect. The article says that before the assembly line, Model Ts were available in other colors, including red, but not after.
Incorrect. Blue is not mentioned as a color for Model Ts.
Incorrect. Green is not mentioned as a color for Model Ts.

questions.question: Who did Henry Ford turn over the company to in 1945?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states, 'He turned over the company to his grandson Henry Ford II in 1945.'
Incorrect. Edsel Ford died in 1943, before 1945.
Incorrect. Clara Bryant was his wife, but there is no mention of her taking over the company.
Incorrect. Thomas Edison was an acquaintance, but he did not take over the company.

questions.question: What did Ford leave most of his wealth to upon his death in 1947?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says, 'Upon his death in 1947, he left most of his wealth to the Ford Foundation.'
Incorrect. He left control of the company to his family, but most of his wealth went to the Ford Foundation.
Incorrect. The Dearborn Independent was his newspaper, but there is no mention of leaving wealth to it.
Incorrect. The League of Nations was promoted by Ford, but there is no mention of leaving wealth to it.
